gaps.note: MegaETH blocks come from a closed JIT executor (F-118). Every check this cycle reached it only through mined transactions: 20,000 replayed transactions and 16,035 blocks of traced against committed state (theme-state-replay), and 19 blocks in the stateless validator (high-throughput). Those transactions are what ordinary users already send. No unit listed which PoolManager branch sides and arithmetic edges the producer has actually executed, so an edge that no user has reached is untested on the code that writes the blocks. The battery and the script sets ran on the replica interpreter, which does not produce blocks (critic query 2026-11-26: mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42@mnet-ash-rpc-2).

The HyperEVM validator is closed and its headers carry no usable state root (F-120). theme-state-replay could compare only the latest value of 3,395 PoolManager words with the official endpoint, because that endpoint ignores the block argument, and theme-hyperevm-twin-state compared 8,464 slots at one block. Both checks see only the last write of each word, over 2,833 mined transactions. Nobody has shown whether eth_call on rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm runs the same EVM that produces blocks, and the 185,529 vector battery counts as validator evidence only if it does.

Polygon, BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche have had no network unit in cycles 22 and 23 (state/ledger.json cells: lastCycle 21). Polygon Salvador and BNB Chain Jenner both activate on 8 December 2026. In cycle 23 only theme-state-replay touched these networks, through mined replays. Critic queries on 2026-11-26: bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org gave Geth/v1.8.2/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 on four of six calls and Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 on two, so two builds sit behind one endpoint. The commit-less build string appears in state/ only once, in an F-139 probe, and no battery run is pinned to it. bsc-rpc.publicnode.com gave reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f/linux. polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com gave bor/280514fa9fb7/v2.11.1-private.

The 19,981 Polygon transactions in theme-state-replay were traced only through polygon.drpc.org, which answers web3_clientVersion with Geth/v10.0.0/drpc (critic query 2026-11-26). That string names no bor build. The committed-state half answered as bor host-85-195-124-57 v2.11.2, a build string that appears in no earlier cycle. The record cannot say which bor build stands behind the Polygon replay.

arbitrum-family says the multi-step replay could not read historical state on Arbitrum One (25 of 25 refused) and that this cycle adds no replay evidence there. theme-state-replay replayed 20,000 Arbitrum One transactions from arbitrum-one-rpc.publicnode.com and arb-one.api.pocket.network, which answered nitro v3.12.2, v3.12.4 and a nitro/vlocal+5f02f3f-modified build. The two units do not contradict each other. Still, the Arbitrum One replay evidence speaks for v3.12.x nodes and not for the rc.9 build (b72783f) that arb1.arbitrum.io reports and whose binaries the network unit read.

The arbitrum-family verifier records that the Go build info of the v3.13.0-b72783f binary names the go-ethereum module as v1.16.2 replaced by ./go-ethereum. The finding and its clearances call the fork v1.17.x, an identification that rests on function line offsets and not on a version string. The cleared items that compare the handlers with v1.17.7 should say this plainly.

Each theme-state-replay window was built from PoolManager logs, so every network reports failedTx 0 (raw/<chain>/result.json). Mined transactions that reverted at top level were never compared with the revert the source gives. A producer that wrongly reverts a burn, take or modifyLiquidity freezes funds, and this replay cannot see that. Transactions that only settle or take native value also have no log, as the unit's own lead says.

The mutation test of theme-state-replay shows that a wrong bitmap bit (flipTick) shows up in only 1 to 5 of 300 transactions per network, and a getAmount0Delta rounding change in 28 to 58. The replay therefore barely tests TickBitmap and the rounding branches of SqrtPriceMath, which are the paths of SAR, SHL, BYTE and the round-up MULMOD. The zero mismatch result should not be read as coverage of those libraries.

Repeated from cycle 22. Every L5 and L6 cell of state/ledger.json is still at lastCycle 1, and no cycle 23 unit worked ordering, reorg depth or producer powers as a question of what a public account can undo.

leads.question: In the MegaETH replica traces of the 20,000 transactions that theme-state-replay replayed (cycles/023/theme-state-replay.work/raw/4326/tx), and in the stateless-validator blocks since cycle 19, which of the conditional jumps in research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json were taken in both directions? Which were taken in one direction only, and which never ran? Report the same for these arithmetic sites: the prod1 != 0 branch of FullMath.mulDiv, the round-up increment of mulDivRoundingUp, both rounding branches of SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown, TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice within 2^16 of MIN_SQRT_PRICE and MAX_SQRT_PRICE, the negative-tick compress path of TickBitmap.position, and BitMath on single high bits. For each site the producer never executed, can an ordinary account reach it in a pool with standard tokens and no hook?
leads.why: The closed JIT has written every MegaETH block, and only mined transactions check it. If a miscompiled edge has never been hit by a user, the first account to send it could misprice its own hookless pool and drain the balance all pools share (A6). This is the Monad coverage method of theme-monad-compiled-coverage applied to the one producer that cannot be rebuilt.

leads.question: Does eth_call on rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm run in the same EVM that produces HyperEVM blocks? Test it with a short probe set whose outcome a revm build and a go-ethereum build would answer differently in non-arithmetic ways. Examples are the error string on a stack underflow, the gas left reported by GAS after a cold SLOAD, and the return data of a failed precompile, or any field a documented API states. Then, over the 2,833 mined PoolManager transactions on the replica (rpc.purroofgroup.com), which jumpmap.json branch sides and FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and TickBitmap edge sites did the validator execute?
leads.why: If eth_call runs the validator's own EVM, the 185,529 vectors cover the validator. If it does not, only 2,833 user transactions do, and the state root cannot catch a validator-only arithmetic fault (F-120).

leads.question: On 8 December 2026 after Jenner (BNB Chain, 02:30 UTC) and Salvador (Polygon, block 98,688,600), which build string does each public endpoint answer? Do battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py give the recorded words, pinned by web3_clientVersion around each batch, on bsc-dataseed1 (both of the builds it rotates), bsc-rpc.publicnode.com and polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com? For Salvador, is any of the five accounts that BlockAlloc rewrites (F-134) a currency of a PoolManager pool, or an address the PoolManager calls in P1 to P3?
leads.why: Both forks bring new client builds that no unit has read, on networks with no network unit since cycle 21. A new opcode or code rewrite fault would be live from that block for any account.

leads.question: On 8 December 2026 after 15:00 UTC (T14), which evm2 revision and ruint version does the Tempo release running on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz pin? Do battery.py, targeted.py, vec/ruintedges.py and script sets 1, 2 and 6 at 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 give the recorded words? Does the release carry the unreleased evm2 main change from wrapping DIV and MOD to ruint checked_div and checked_rem, and do the division-by-zero vectors still return 0?
leads.why: Tempo runs a single client, so a fault there is the network's answer. stablecoin-l1 found the DIV and MOD rewrite on evm2 main this cycle. FullMath, UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp and SqrtPriceMath depend on DIV and MOD at zero and at the edges (src/libraries/FullMath.sol, src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol). This carries L-936 forward.

leads.question: Avalanche folds storage slot S and S with bit 248 flipped into one entry (F-040). Does any other client on the list transform or bucket storage keys before they reach its state store, so that two (address, slot) pairs or a persistent and a transient slot can share one entry? Read MegaETH's SALT bucket mapping in mega-evm and the stateless validator, Monad's TrieDb key encoding and its state cache (category/execution/ethereum/db), and nanoreth's state patches. For each, can an ordinary account choose a slot of its own contract that lands on a PoolManager slot?
leads.why: A key transform that aliases slots across accounts would let an attacker overwrite pool or ERC-6909 storage. The Avalanche fold was found in a client, and no unit has looked for its kind on the other custom state stores.

leads.question: Why did 3,135 of the 20,000 replayed MegaETH transactions contain a PoolManager frame that reverted and was caught, against 2 to 165 on the other nine networks (raw/<chain>/result.json, counts pm-frame-reverted)? Group the reverts by revert data and by the PoolManager pc where each started. Does any of them come from a MegaETH resource limit (compute gas, KV update or data size limits in mega-evm limit.rs) and not from a source revert, and can such a limit stop a frame after take and before settle?
leads.why: A revert rate six to sixty times the other networks is the one anomaly in the replay. A frame stopped by a resource limit is a network behaviour that the source does not model.

leads.question: Over the same windows, list the mined transactions to the PoolManager or to its routers with receipt status 0, from trace_filter or from block bodies. Does the replay model give the same revert, at the same frame, from the parent-block state?
leads.why: The log-based windows leave out every failed transaction (failedTx 0 everywhere). A producer that reverts a valid burn, take or liquidity removal is a freeze that only shows up there.

leads.question: Which source does the commit-less Geth/v1.8.2/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 build on bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org come from, and what did reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f change from v0.1.4 in the opcode, precompile and state paths? Rerun battery.py and targeted.py while bracketing every batch with web3_clientVersion until each of the two dataseed builds has answered the full set.
leads.why: Two builds rotate behind one endpoint (critic queries 2026-11-26), and results so far cannot be tied to one of them. BNB validators run builds that no one can read (F-121).

Which operator runs the nitro/vlocal+5f02f3f-modified build that pocket answered with, and do its answers differ from v3.12.4 on the battery?

leads.question: Find a Polygon trace endpoint whose web3_clientVersion names a bor build, and rerun the theme-state-replay window and script set 1, which has not finished since cycle 21, pinned to that build and to bor/280514fa9fb7.
leads.why: The Polygon replay ran on the drpc aggregator, whose client is hidden, and four private bor commits have answered with no pinned run.

leads.question: From the 60,000 replayed transactions on Base, Monad and MegaETH, select every transaction that flips a tick bitmap bit, crosses a bitmap word boundary, or takes a round-up branch in SqrtPriceMath. Rerun scripts/mutate.py on that subset only. Are the detection rates for flipTick and getAmount0Delta then above 90 percent?
leads.why: With 1 to 5 of 300 detections today, the zero mismatch result says almost nothing about TickBitmap and rounding. A targeted subset would make the mined replay test the SAR, SHL and round-up MULMOD paths.

leads.question: Does HyperCore accept an address that has EVM code, in particular a contract it did not deploy, as the AQAv2 treasury address of a token? Is there any path other than authorizeAqav2Role signed by a staked deployer plus a validator vote that sets it? Answer from the Hyperliquid API reference and the AQAv2 documentation.
leads.why: This one fact settles F-020 (plausible, operator, high). It cannot raise the actor to unprivileged unless an unstaked path exists.

leads.question: In what order does the MegaETH sequencer reconsider candidates that BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT skipped, according to its documentation, the realtime API page or the mega-evm limit.rs comments?
leads.why: This one fact settles F-062 (plausible, unprivileged, low). It decides whether one ordinary account can delay a chosen exit by more than one block.

leads.question: Does category/vm/compiler/ir/basic_blocks.cpp at v0.16.7 decode bytes e6, e7 and e8 with an allowed or a disallowed immediate the same way as the interpreter and EIP-8024, and does rpc.monad.xyz run with trace_calls (interpreter only) or with the dual VM?
leads.why: Only the second half bears on PoolManager evidence: it decides whether committed-state comparisons on Monad are interpreter against interpreter. The first half matters for hooks once MONAD_NEXT_AMSTERDAM is scheduled.

leads.question: Does the theme-state-replay word-by-word replay hold on the eleven networks it skipped? Use trace endpoints where they exist, and the cycle 21 parent-storage replay for Arc, Elysium and Tempo.
leads.why: Arc, Elysium and Tempo run code that is not public or has only one client, and none of them has a word-by-word replay. The other eight have one only through earlier swap checks.

leads.question: Which Ethereum hard fork after Fusaka is scheduled with a mainnet date, and which of its EIPs does each OP Stack and Nitro release already carry in dormant form? Does any of them change an opcode result, a call's return data, the 63/64 forwarding or the gas left at a hook or token call in a way that changes a PoolManager outcome, not only its gas?
leads.why: Nitro v3.13.0 already carries dormant Amsterdam rules (arbitrum-family). Ethereum has had no network unit since cycle 21, and the upcoming-forks angle was not given to chain 1 or the OP Stack in cycle 23.
